_doc: Every tester under 9_others/test/ that no workflow names by filename. lint-pipeline.yml registers its testers as hand-written YAML steps, one per tester; a tester added without that step is committed, looks like coverage in a directory listing, and is executed by nothing. 43 of the 101 testers were in that state on 2026-09-16 (ticket #368). This file is the second registry, and unlike the YAML it is data: 9_others/test/run-registered-testers.sh executes what is listed here, and 9_others/test/test_every_tester_is_registered.sh fails when a tester appears under 9_others/test/ that is named neither by a workflow nor by this file. Add new testers HERE, never as another YAML step. Testers that do not live under 9_others/test/ (e.g. the b_infra protection suite) are registered the same way, with an optional "path" (repo-root-relative) telling the runner where the file is; without a path the runner assumes 9_others/test/NAME.
_doc_status: run = executed, failure is fatal. quarantine = executed, and asserted to STILL FAIL: if a quarantined tester starts passing, run-registered-testers.sh goes RED and tells you to flip it to run. A quarantine can therefore never rot into a silent skip, and there is no status that swallows an exit code — that is deliberate, it is the defect ticket #368 exists to undo.
_doc_why: Eight of the ten quarantined entries below name a production incident in their own header, with the GitHub run id. They were written as the fix for that incident and then never connected to a runner, so the incident they guard has been unguarded ever since. A red entry here is a real defect with an owner to find, not a tester to silence.

cgc-db-package.test.sh.reason: X2-F1 (#368): gate_repo_push case G fails — 'first publish of a PUBLIC repo's package needs GITHUB_TOKEN in env'. Still fails with GITHUB_TOKEN populated, so it is the tester's stub env or the gate's precedence, not a missing secret. 32 of 33 cases pass.

test_build_schema_api_mcp.sh.reason: X2-F2 (#368): checks 3/4/8 shell out to validate-build-schema.ts, which imports 'ajv'. lint-pipeline.yml has no setup-node and no npm ci, so this cannot pass on the runner as the pipeline stands. Needs a deps step before it can be promoted.

test_c3_services_api_registry.sh.reason: X2-F3 (#368): two real failures. (5) stdio-only MCP cloud-vault-mcp is in the registry with has_mcp=true, expected false. (6) shares the ajv dependency of X2-F2. Checks 1-4 pass.

test_docker_npm_baked_into_image.sh.reason: X2-F11 (#368): needs the unix repo (checked ~/git/cloud-infra-desktop and the II_Unix submodule) and finds neither. lint-pipeline.yml's init-submodules step includes only I_cloud, so this cannot resolve on the runner as the pipeline stands. Found by test_every_tester_is_registered.sh on its very first run — my own sweep had credited a prose mention in 9_others/src/ensure-deps.sh:125 as a reference.

test_gateway_routes_goose.sh.reason: X2-F5 (#368): a_solutions/user-ai_my-ai-api/src/code/gateway.mjs is 2059 bytes and contains zero occurrences of routeToGoose. Checks C/D/E/F all fail. Either the goose routing was removed, or the tester was written for a feature that never landed. Needs an owner's call, not a patch.

test_service_header_present.sh.reason: X2-F12 (#372, D3): the VACUITY is fixed — the tester now FAILS when a declared scope is unreachable or contributes zero files (proven: rc 0 -> 1 with a_solutions/ absent). It stays RED for the real reason, and the real reason is not 'a lost banner': a_solutions/user-comm_chat-mattermost/dist/code/arm64/Dockerfile IS stamped, by the OTHER engine. cloud-u-containers/_shared/engine.nix hardcoded a different wording than the canonical .marker in 9_others/src/generated-header.json, and 255 container dist/ files carry it. engine.nix is FIXED to emit the canonical marker (cloud-u-containers), and test_container_engine_marker_matches.sh now guards the agreement. This entry must stay quarantined until someone runs a nix container build: dist/ is compiled output, no workflow in cloud-u-containers regenerates it, and this container has no nix. When that build lands this goes green and the quarantine assertion will say so.

test_ship_workflows_dual_trigger.sh.reason: X2-F10 (#372, D3): PARTIALLY FIXED, deliberately still red. ship-wrangler.yml was a REAL cascade gap and is fixed: it now has the workflow_run trigger on 'Ship -> gen-configs (cloud-data)', the if-gate on workflow_run.conclusion, and 1_cloud-configs/dist/build-*.json in its push paths. Evidence it was real: infra-cloud_cloudflare-worker/src/build-cloudflare-worker.json is a symlink to ../../../1_cloud-configs/dist/build-cloudflare-worker.json, so a regenerated config shipped everywhere else and never reached the worker. STILL RED for ship-cgc-db-seed.yml, ship-reconcile.yml and ship-reports.yml, and that needs an OWNER'S DECISION rather than a patch: the tester applies a blanket 'every ship*.yml must cascade off gen-configs' rule, and none of those three references 1_cloud-configs/dist or gen-configs at all (comment-stripped count = 0 for each). ship-reconcile dispatches ship.yml for drifted services, and ship.yml already cascades, so cascading reconcile too looks redundant by design. ship-cgc-db-seed.yml belongs to ticket #352's owner. I did not narrow the tester to make it green: if those three are genuinely out of scope the RULE should become data-driven (cascade required only for config consumers), and that is a decision for whoever owns the ship topology.
